correctness.rationale: For all integers q>=2 the target edge set is exactly the ternary equality pattern with two equal symbols. Direct degree checks and a two-step diagonal communication argument show the q^2-vertex de Bruijn subgraph is balanced and strongly connected. Every cyclic universal word anchors uniquely at the edge 001. BEST counts the rooted circuits as tau*((q-2)!)^q. The off-diagonal Laplacian block has determinant 3^binom(q,2) and inverse (2I+R)/3; its diagonal Schur complement equals (2/3)(qI-J), whose cofactor is (2/3)^(q-1)*q^(q-2). Thus tau=2^(q-1)3^((q-1)(q-2)/2)q^(q-2), proving the stated closed formula without computational dependence. An independent exact Bareiss cofactor implementation verifies q=2..8, explicit constructive windows verify q=2..25, and complete anchored tour enumeration verifies the cycle counts 2,36,55296 for q=2,3,4. Finite checks do not prove the infinite theorem; all critical nonstandard steps are reconstructed in RESULT.md and implemented in verify.py.

value.rationale: The exactly-two-equal triple language is a natural complete nontrivial equality-pattern slice of q-ary length-three words (neither all-distinct nor constant), motivating a shortest exact factor listing for all labeled alphabets. The theorem counts all such universal cycles, not merely existence, for every q>=2, revealing a non-obvious factorial/power product through the spanning-arborescence structure of a q^2-vertex directed overlap graph. The result gives exact design-space size and symbol balance for locally constrained sequence constructions; the nontrivial all-q determinant evaluation and full exact classification exceed a routine numeric or renaming exercise. No claim of improved generic cycle-counting methods is made.
